description: GCP: cache the gapic (gRPC channel-holding) clients in GcpClientProvider via a ConcurrentHashMap keyed clientType+':'+projectId (computeIfAbsent), mirroring the AWS provider, so each long-lived gapic client is built once and reused instead of leaking channel threads across ~207 never-closed call sites. Fix the 6 caller sites that currently close a provider client via try-with-resources (which would close the now-shared instance). Independent of FEAT-001 (AWS) and FEAT-002 (Azure) — different files.
steps: Read xamops-service/src/main/java/com/xammer/cloud/service/gcp/GcpClientProvider.java first (and context.json). Add 'private final Map<String,Object> clientCache = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();' and a private helper such as getOrCreate(String type, String projectId, Supplier<T> factory) that returns the cached instance via computeIfAbsent and never caches a null.

Convert every gapic getter (those that call XxxClient.create(settings)) to cache its result keyed 'XxxClient:'+gcpProjectId (RecommenderClientForBillingAccount keyed on billingAccountId). Preserve the Optional contract: empty when getCredentials(projectId) is empty; keep the per-method catch (IOException e){ log.error(...); return null; } inside the create lambda and ensure a null create result is NOT inserted into the cache. Apply to: Asset, CloudBuild, FunctionService, IAM, KeyManagement, Routers, Routes, SecretManager, SecurityPolicies, Recommender, RecommenderForBillingAccount, SecurityCenterV2, Instances, ZoneOperations, MetricService, Networks, Subnetworks, ClusterManager, Projects, OrgPolicy, CloudBilling, CloudCatalog, BudgetService, ForwardingRules, Firewalls, Disks, Snapshots, Addresses, Images, CloudRunServices, CloudRedis, ApiGatewayService, AppEngineServices, Config, RegionCommitments, VertexAIModel, VertexAIEndpoint, PubSubTopic, PubSubSubscription, MonitoringAlert, MonitoringUptime, Dataplex, Scheduler, AlertPolicy, OsConfig, BigQueryReservation, Regions, InstanceGroupManagers, RegionInstanceGroupManagers, InstanceTemplates, RegionInstanceTemplates, Autoscalers, RegionAutoscalers, TargetHttpsProxies, TargetSslProxies, SslCertificates, VpnTunnels, TargetPools, ArtifactRegistry, Dns.

Leave the lightweight getters alone with a short comment noting the decision: getStorageClient and getBigQueryClient (Options.getService(), no gapic channel) and getSqlAdminClient (SQLAdmin over GoogleNetHttpTransport, no gapic channel). Leave validateServiceAccountAccess exactly as-is — it correctly closes its own one-shot non-cached ProjectsClient via try-with-resources.

Fix the 6 caller sites that close a now-shared cached client: change 'try (XxxClient c = provider.getXxxClient(...).get()) { ... }' to fetch and use the client without closing it. Sites: service/gcp/GcpBudgetService.java ~201, ~341, ~509 (BudgetServiceClient); service/gcp/GcpDataService.java ~955 (IAMClient); service/gcp/GcpOptimizationService.java ~3503 (TargetHttpsProxiesClient) and ~3595 (TargetPoolsClient).

Re-run grep 'try\s*\(.*get[A-Za-z0-9]+Client' under xamops-service/src/main to confirm the only remaining provider-client try-with-resources is GcpClientProvider.validateServiceAccountAccess (which stays).

Add a unit test xamops-service/src/test/java/com/xammer/cloud/service/gcp/GcpClientProviderCachingTest.java: construct GcpClientProvider with a mocked CloudAccountRepository + PermissionGapRegistry; for a project with a well-formed fake SA key JSON, assert two calls to a representative gapic getter (e.g. getRecommenderClient) return the same unwrapped instance, and that a project with no credentials returns Optional.empty(). If a usable fake SA key for GoogleCredentials.fromStream is infeasible, assert caching via a provider spy / the cache map instead and record the limitation in findings.
acceptance_criteria: GcpClientProvider holds a ConcurrentHashMap client cache and every gapic getter returns a cached instance via computeIfAbsent (second call returns the same object).
Lightweight getters (Storage, BigQuery, SqlAdmin) and validateServiceAccountAccess are unchanged, each with a brief comment where a decision was made.
The Optional contract and per-method IOException logging are preserved; a failed create returns Optional.empty() and is not cached.
No caller closes a cached provider client (the 6 try-with-resources sites are converted); only validateServiceAccountAccess still closes its own non-cached client.
findings: RESOLVED via decision D (do NOT cache GCP clients). During implementation of the FEAT's original plan I found the scope was wrong: caching the gapic clients is UNSAFE because ~97 active try-with-resources call sites across the gcp package close a client obtained from a GcpClientProvider getter (the FEAT's verification grep only catches 6 of them because it keys on an inline getXxxClient(...) in the try header; the other ~91 assign clientOpt.get() to a typed local and are invisible to that pattern). Caching + closing at those sites would close the shared instance after first use and regress most GCP dashboards. Parent decision: REVERT the GcpClientProvider caching entirely and keep the existing per-call XxxClient.create(settings) returning Optional pattern, because that pattern already CLOSES every gapic client via try-with-resources at the call site, so GCP is already leak-safe for gRPC-channel threads and is NOT a dominant leak source (the real leaks were AWS sdk-ScheduledExecutor [FEAT-001] and Azure per-call HttpClient [FEAT-002]). Actions taken: (1) git checkout reverted GcpClientProvider.java, GcpBudgetService.java, GcpDataService.java back to HEAD (working tree clean, no caching changes remain); @Cacheable on credentials and validateServiceAccountAccess left as the original code. (2) No GcpClientProviderCachingTest added. (3) Scanned the gcp (and war/gcp) packages for any gapic client created WITHOUT being closed or returned to a closing caller: grep for 'XxxClient.create(' outside GcpClientProvider found ZERO matches — every gapic client is created only in the provider, returned as Optional, and closed by the caller via try-with-resources. The only direct client handle outside the provider is CspBillingQueryService.buildClient() -> BigQueryOptions...getService(), which is a lightweight HTTP BigQuery handle (no gRPC channel / executor threads), so it is not a gRPC-channel leak. Conclusion: no un-closed GCP client creation found; GCP already leak-safe via try-with-resources — no GCP code change needed. Verification: 'mvn -q -pl xamops-service -am compile' succeeded; GCP test suite (com.xammer.cloud.service.gcp.*Test + GcpDenialClassifierTest + GcpAutoSpottingControllerTest) ran 160 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors. FEAT-001 (AWS) and FEAT-002 (Azure) commits left untouched.
